description:
FILED s470bx (Opus, 2026-09-06) while closing #1231 + #1044.  PRE-EXISTING and
deliberately out of that change's scope: #1231/#1044 fixed the EXPR handle
slots (`stat`, `lstat`, the 26 filetests); this is rule (a) of #1044's own
addendum, which is about the GLOB slots and applies to them too.

THE RULE.  A `()`-PROTOTYPE sub â `use constant` included â is INLINED by
perl's parser before ANY of these slots sees it, so the handle is named by the
constant's VALUE.  An ORDINARY sub in a GLOB slot is NOT called and does not
displace the bareword.  #1044's addendum proved that with the warning TEXT as
the discriminator (`tell CPATH` warns "on unopened filehandle YYPATH", i.e.
the constant RAN; `tell SPATH` warns "on unopened filehandle " with an empty
name, i.e. it did not).

PCL EMITS NO WARNINGS (#221), so the warning text is not observable here.
Re-probed through BEHAVIOUR instead (scratch/s470bx/p1291b.pl), perl 5.40.3 vs
PCL at s470bx's HEAD:

    use constant CPATH => 'YYPATH';
    open(YYPATH, '<', '/etc/passwd') or die;
    close(CPATH);
    print fileno(YYPATH);                      perl: UNDEF   PCL: 5
    open(ZZP, â¦); use constant ZPATH => 'ZZP';
    print eof(ZPATH);                          perl: 0       PCL: 1
    print tell(ZPATH);                         perl: 0       PCL: -1

So `close(CPATH)` closes NOTHING in PCL, and `eof`/`tell` answer as for an
unopened handle: the bareword CPATH goes into the slot verbatim instead of
being replaced by the constant's value.  The same is expected of `binmode`,
`seek`, `fileno`, `truncate`, `flock`, the `read`/`sysread`/`syswrite` family
and the `open` family â every entry of
`Pl::Environment::_builtin_prototypes` â but only the four above were
measured.

WHERE IT SITS.  `_read_star_slot_bareword`'s builtin half is the one place
that decides what a bareword in a `*` slot becomes.  It now knows about the
EXPR/GLOB split (the `expr_slot` flag added by #1044), and this is the
remaining axis: a `()`-prototype name should be INLINED to its value FIRST, in
both kinds of slot, before that split is even asked.  `Pl::Environment`'s
constants table already knows which names are inlinable, which is what makes
this a compiler-side change and not a runtime one.

MEASURE FIRST, as #1044's addendum instructs: `use constant` names in a handle
slot may well be commoner than declared subs there, but nobody has counted.
The count is a scan of the five populations for a bareword in a glob slot
whose name is a known constant; #1044's own scan (2412 bareword operand slots
over 1452 files) found ZERO for the EXPR-slot question, so do not assume this
one is bigger without the number.
subject: A ()-prototype sub / `use constant` in a GLOB handle slot is not INLINED â `close(CPATH)` closes nothing (#1044 addendum rule (a))
